messages:
Sam: quick readout from the Starlark-7B onboarding smoke — sharing a micro-snapshot of cost vs quality so product/GTN can decide next steps. TL;DR: int8 gives ~2.8x cost savings vs fp16 with ~1.8% QA-F1 drop on our passage QA slice; int4 drops another 1.6% but latency tail gets worse.
Priya: can you drop the unit econ numbers? we need per-1k-token pricing to compare to routing floor.
Sam: sure — rough running numbers from dedicated test pool (eu-west):
Sam:   • fp16: $0.42 per 1k tokens, p50=45ms, p95=220ms
Sam:   • int8: $0.15 per 1k tokens, p50=42ms, p95=260ms
Sam:   • int4 (aggressive): $0.08 per 1k tokens, p50=40ms, p95=410ms
Elle: wow p95 for int4 is pretty bad. what's causing the tail? kernel scheduling or KV cache miss amplification?
Omar: from infra traces it's KV cache eviction spikes when prefix lengths > 1024. int4 increases memory pressure and we see more swapping across worker shards — manifests as long tails.
Priya: what's the impact on QA accuracy for the product-critical slice? precise numbers please.
Sam: QA metrics on our benchmark subset (multi-turn, high-context):
Sam:   • fp16: F1=81.7, ROUGE-L=42.1, hallucination rate~3.2%
Sam:   • int8: F1=80.1, ROUGE-L=41.4, hallucination rate~3.8%
Sam:   • int4: F1=78.5, ROUGE-L=40.2, hallucination rate~5.1%
Priya: product asks what to do for GTN pilot (targeting conversational search). tradeoff threshold: <1% F1 drop is acceptable.
Elle: so int8 is borderline (1.6% drop) — does priming/adapter tuning recover some of that?
Sam: tried light priming and a 200-example distillation pass on int8 — recovered ~0.6% F1 but added +0.02ms token cost (negligible).
Omar: operationally, int8 increases p95 latency by ~15% vs fp16 under bursty traffic; could violate SLO for chat routes. but routing by tail budget could mitigate via hybrid routing.
Priya: can you sketch a recommended rollout? product needs a short playbook they can follow.
Sam: recommendation (concise):
Sam:   1) Start GTN pilot on int8 with conservative routing: route 90% to int8, 10% to fp16 for canary, monitor QA slices + 95th tail.
Sam:   2) Enable prefix-KV warmstart for long-context users to reduce int4/int8 tail impact.
Sam:   3) If p95>300ms for chat, fallback to fp16 for that user session.
Sam:   4) Do a 1-week distillation/priming sweep to see if int8 parity improves to <=1% F1 gap.
Elle: agree. add automated eval hooks (daily) against the product's golden prompts and an alert if hallucination rate rises >1%.
Priya: what about cost savings delta vs expected ARR impact? need a one-liner for GTN pitch.
Sam: quick calc: if average session is 1.2k tokens, int8 saves ~$0.33 per session vs fp16. at scale 10k sessions/day that's ~$99k/mo. caveat: SLA/regression risk if we push too hard.
Omar: CI-bot: scheduled smoke tests for Starlark-7B int8 are green  — see build 2026-03-12T09:14Z :white_check_mark:
CI-bot: link: https://internal-ci.redwood/jobs/12345
Priya: thanks. next steps: draft a short pilot checklist for GTN (can someone draft and tag me)?
Elle: I'll put together the checklist with the routing flags and daily eval hooks, pinging you by EOD.
Sam: attaching quick config snippet we used for hybrid canary:
Sam: ```
Sam: routing: 
Sam:   - route: starlark-7b-int8
Sam:     pct: 90
Sam:     fallback: starlark-7b-fp16
Sam:     tail_budget_ms: 300
Sam:   - route: starlark-7b-fp16
Sam:     pct: 10
Sam: ```
Priya: perfect. can we also include a short note on priming/distillation ops impact on infra cost?
Sam: yes — distillation runs we did added ~3% training infra overhead for a 0.6% F1 gain; recommend running distill in batch off-peak windows.
Elle: I'll draft the one-pager for GTN: includes unit econ table, rollout steps, and an ops checklist. will post in #product when ready. :+1:
Omar: one more ops note — if we enable int4 in the future, we need to bump worker memory or shard differently to avoid KV eviction tail.
Priya: thanks everyone. closing the loop: I'll share the pilot request with GTN and link back to Elle's checklist once available.
Sam: thanks — leaving the thread open for any late questions.
